mainTopic: Whether the protection of sold property extends to gifts, and why sold property is not taken to pay for lost produce.
overview: This amud opens by finishing an earlier point: the special protections for יתומים cover adult orphans too, not only young ones. Then רב אחדבוי בר אמי asks whether the משנה's rule (a creditor may not take sold property while the debtor still has free property) also protects someone who received the land as a מתנה. מר קשישא tries to prove that it does, from a ברייתא about a שכיב מרע who gave gifts in order: the creditor collects from the last gift, even if it is the worst land. The גמרא pushes this proof away in three ways. The ברייתא may be about paying creditors, not gifts. Or 'collects from the last' may only mean the last one ends up losing. Or all the fields may have been the same quality. Next the גמרא asks why sold property is not taken to pay for lost produce. עולא and רבי יוחנן say it is because the produce is not written, and they defend this reason against a challenge from the support of a wife and daughters. רבי חנינא gives a different reason: the amount of produce is not fixed. The amud ends as the גמרא begins to ask whether רבי חנינא needs both 'fixed' and 'written'; that question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The orphans' protections apply to adult orphans too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא clarifies that the special protections for יתומים cover adult orphans, and of course minors, both for the oath rule and the inferior-land rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the חכמים spoke about orphans, they meant even adult orphans, and certainly young ones. This is true both for the oath and for collecting from the worst land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes an earlier discussion by explaining which יתומים get the special protections: adults as well as minors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two rules protect orphans: a creditor must take a שבועה before collecting from them, and he collects only from זיבורית (the worst land). A learner might think these protections are only for helpless young children. The גמרא says no: the word יתומים here includes adults, and minors are obviously included.

keyTerms.meaning: Orphans; here, heirs whose father died owing a debt

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'needless to say minors' as meaning minors are the main case. The new point is that ADULT orphans are included; minors are the obvious case.

phrases.english: The orphans of which they spoke
means adults, and needless to say minors
whether for the oath or for inferior-quality land
phrases.notes: Two separate protections: the creditor must swear before collecting from orphans, and he may collect only from their worst land.

steps.triggerLanguage: יתומין שאמרו גדולים ואין צריך לומר קטנים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the previous discussion about debts collected from orphans.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The orphan protections (oath and inferior land) apply to adult orphans as well as minors.

steps.title: The משנה's rule: don't take sold property while free property remains
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: a creditor may not collect from נכסים משועבדים while the debtor still has בני חורין.
steps.simpleTranslation: A creditor does not collect from land the debtor already sold to others, as long as the debtor still owns other free land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and quotes it. This is setting up the question that comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A loan puts a lien on the borrower's land, so a creditor can sometimes take it back even from a buyer. The משנה limits this: if the borrower still has his own free land, even poor land, the creditor must take from that and leave the buyers alone.

keyTerms.meaning: Liened property that the debtor already sold to someone else
Free property still owned by the debtor

steps.whyThisMatters: This basic rule is the foundation for the whole question about gifts that follows.

phrases.english: Payment is not collected from liened property
where there is free property

steps.triggerLanguage: אין נפרעין מנכסים משועבדים במקום שיש בני חורין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A creditor may not collect from sold, liened property while the debtor still has free property.

steps.title: What about property that was given as a gift?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחדבוי בר אמי asks whether the משנה's rule also protects someone who received the land as a מתנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחדבוי בר אמי asked: what is the law when the debtor gave the land away as a gift?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question is raised: does the משנה's rule apply when the land was given away free instead of sold?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה talks about property that was sold to buyers. Here the debtor gave the land away. The question is whether the gift-receiver is also protected while the debtor still has free land.

keyTerms.meaning: How is it? What is the law?

phrases.english: Rav Aḥadevoi bar Ami asked:
What about a gift?

steps.triggerLanguage: בעי רב אחדבוי בר אמי במתנה היאך
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how far the משנה's rule reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the rule against collecting from liened property while free property exists also protect a gift-receiver?

steps.title: The two sides of the gift question
steps.stepSummary: Is the rule only to protect buyers from losing their money, or is a gift-receiver like a buyer because the giver got some benefit?
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe the חכמים made this rule only so buyers wouldn't lose money, and a gift-receiver paid nothing, so the rule does not apply. Or maybe a gift is also included, because nobody gives a gift unless he gets some benefit from the person, so it is like a buyer's loss.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the question is hard by laying out two possible ways of seeing it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: the rule is a תקנה to prevent פסידא דלקוחות, the loss of buyers who paid money. A gift-receiver paid nothing, so he loses nothing real. Side two: a giver always gets something back from the receiver, like goodwill, so the receiver is a kind of buyer and deserves the same protection.

keyTerms.meaning: An enactment made by the חכמים

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the reason behind the משנה's rule decides how far it reaches.

phrases.english: Is it an enactment that the Rabbis made
because of the buyers' loss,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מַתָּנָה, דְּלֵיכָּא פְּסֵידָא דְלָקוֹחוֹת – לָא;
phrases.english: but a gift, where there is no buyers' loss, is not included;
or perhaps a gift is included too,

phrases.aramaic: אִי לָאו דְּאִית לֵיהּ הֲנָאָה מִינֵּיהּ –
phrases.english: since if he did not get some benefit from him
he would not have given him a gift,
and therefore it is like the buyers' loss?

steps.triggerLanguage: תקנתא הוא דעבוד רבנן משום פסידא דלקוחות
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the reasoning on both sides of the question from Step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the rule's purpose only to protect paying buyers, or does it cover anyone who received the land, since a giver always gets some benefit?

steps.title: A proof from a dying man's gifts
steps.stepSummary: מר קשישא brings a ברייתא: when a שכיב מרע gives several money gifts, nobody counts as first, so a creditor collects from all of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר קשישא son of רב חסדא said to רב אשי: Come and hear. A dying man said, 'Give 200 זוז to this person, 300 to that one, and 400 to another.' We don't say whoever was named first gets it first. So if a loan document turns up against the dying man, the creditor collects from all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: מר קשישא quotes a ברייתא to try to answer the gift question. Here the ברייתא is only quoted; step 7 shows what it proves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שכיב מרע's gifts all take effect together when he dies, so no receiver is earlier than another. Because of that, a creditor who appears takes from all the receivers together. Since this ברייתא deals with gift-receivers facing a creditor, מר קשישא thinks it can settle רב אחדבוי's question.

keyTerms.meaning: The one listed first in the document

steps.confusionAlert: Don't jump ahead and decide the question is already answered. The ברייתא is only quoted here; the גמרא explains what it proves in step 7.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר קַשִּׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא לְרַב אָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: Mar Kashisha, son of Rav Ḥisda, said to Rav Ashi:
Come and hear: a man on his deathbed who said:
"Give two hundred zuz to so-and-so,
and three hundred to so-and-so,
and four hundred to so-and-so" –

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אוֹמְרִים: כׇּל הַקּוֹדֵם בִּשְׁטָר זָכָה;
phrases.english: we do not say: whoever comes first in the document acquires;
therefore, if a loan document came out against him –
he collects from all of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה מר קשישא בריה דרב חסדא לרב אשי תא שמע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to settle the gift question from Steps 3–4 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: Whether the protection for liened property covers gift-receivers.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a שכיב מרע who gives several money gifts, where a creditor collects from all the receivers together.

steps.title: The second half of the ברייתא: gifts listed in order
steps.stepSummary: If the שכיב מרע listed the gifts one after another, whoever comes first in the document wins, so a creditor collects from the last gift first, then the one before it, and so on.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he said: 'Give two hundred זוז to this person, and after him to this one, and after him to this one,' we say whoever comes first in the document acquires first. So if a loan document comes out against the giver, the creditor collects from the last one. If the last one doesn't have enough, he collects from the one before. If that one doesn't have enough, he collects from the one before that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the same ברייתא from step 5, now giving the opposite case, where the gifts are given in a clear order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5 the gifts were all given together, so nobody was first and the creditor took from everyone. Here there is an order, so the earlier receivers are protected and the creditor starts with the last one. This sets up the proof the גמרא will draw in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And after him, to so-and-so (the gifts are given in order)
Whoever comes first in the document acquires first
He collects from the last one

phrases.english: But if he said:
"Give two hundred zuz to so-and-so,
and after him to so-and-so, and after him to so-and-so" –
we say: whoever comes first in the document acquires.
phrases.notes: The 'document' is the written list of the שכיב מרע's gifts.

phrases.english: Therefore, if a loan document came out against him –
he collects from the last one.
If he does not have enough, he collects from the one before him.
If he does not have enough, he collects from the one before that.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל אִם אָמַר תְּנוּ מָאתַיִם זוּז לִפְלוֹנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא begun in step 5 with the contrasting case of ordered gifts.
steps.raayaObject: Whether the תקנה of not collecting from משועבדים when בני חורין exist also covers gift-receivers.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the שכיב מרע's ordered money gifts, brought by מר קשישא.

steps.title: The proof: the creditor must take the worse land from the last gift
steps.stepSummary: Even if the first gift is medium land and the last is the worst land, the creditor collects from the worst land. So the רבנן made the תקנה for gifts too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even though the first gift is medium-quality land and the last is the worst land, he collects from the worst land and not from the medium land. Learn from this: the רבנן made their תקנה for gifts too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the ברייתא: the תקנה that protects buyers also protects people who received a gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A creditor is normally entitled to medium-quality land, so being forced to take the worst land must come from a special rule. The rule is that the later gift still belonged to the giver when the earlier gift was given, so it counts as בני חורין compared to the earlier one. That is the same תקנה as for buyers, now applied to a מתנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it (a conclusion is being drawn)

phrases.english: And even though the first one has medium land
and the last one has the worst land –
he collects from the worst land, he does not collect from the medium land.
Learn from this:
for a gift too, the Rabbis made the enactment.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּקַמָּא בֵּינוֹנִית וּבָתְרָא זִיבּוּרִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the answer to רב אחדבוי בר אמי's question out of the ברייתא quoted in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That a gift-receiver is protected by the תקנה just like a buyer.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The creditor collects worst land from the last gift instead of medium land from the first.

steps.title: Pushing back: the case is about creditors, not gifts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof by saying the ברייתא is about a man paying back his creditors, not giving gifts.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? A case of creditors.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from step 7 by reading the ברייתא differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the people on the list are creditors being paid back, then each of them is like a buyer who gave something of value. The תקנה for buyers clearly applies to them, so the ברייתא says nothing about plain gifts.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (a new reading of a source)

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here? –
With a creditor.
phrases.notes: He means the dying man is splitting his money among people he owes, to pay them back.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 7 by moving the ברייתא to a different case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the ברייתא about gifts.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא may be about creditors, who are like buyers, so it tells us nothing about gifts.

steps.title: Challenge: the word ״תְּנוּ״ sounds like a gift
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the ברייתא says ״תְּנוּ״ (give), which sounds like a gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he said 'Give'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading from step 8 using the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״תְּנוּ״ is the usual way to hand out a gift. So how can the ברייתא be about paying debts?

keyTerms.meaning: Give (the word used in the ברייתא)
But it says! (pointing to words in a source)

phrases.english: But he said "Give"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא תְּנוּ קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the creditor reading of step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא is about creditors.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wording ״תְּנוּ״ points to giving a gift, not paying a debt.

steps.title: Answer: ״תְּנוּ״ means give it for my debt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that ״תְּנוּ״ means 'give it as payment for my debt.'
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Give' for my debt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the creditor reading by explaining the word ״תְּנוּ״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״תְּנוּ״ can also mean 'hand over the money I owe.' So the wording fits paying creditors just fine.

phrases.english: "Give" for my debt.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנוּ בְּחוֹבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״תְּנוּ״ means give as payment for my debt.

steps.title: Challenge: just check whose loan document is earlier
steps.stepSummary: If they are creditors, the order should depend on whose loan document is dated earlier, not on the order the dying man listed them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let's just look at whose document comes first!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem with the creditor reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Among creditors, the one whose loan came first collects first. So why would the order in the dying man's instructions matter at all?

phrases.english: But let us see whose document comes first!
phrases.notes: He means the loan documents, which have dates on them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִיחְזֵי שְׁטָרָא דְּמַאן קָדֵים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second attack on the creditor reading, now on the legal outcome.
steps.kashyaTarget: The creditor reading of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With creditors, the dates on the loan documents decide the order, not the dying man's list.

steps.title: Answer: there are no loan documents
steps.stepSummary: The case is one where the creditors have no loan documents.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is no document.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that there are no loan documents to compare.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With no dated loan documents, for example if they were lost, we can't tell whose loan came first. So the order the dying man gave is all we have to go on.

phrases.english: Where there is no document.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּלֵיכָּא שְׁטָרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The creditors have dated loan documents.
steps.terutzMaskana: The creditors have no loan documents, so the dying man's order decides.

steps.title: Challenge: the ברייתא mentions a document
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says 'whoever comes first in the document,' so there must be a document.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it says 'whoever comes first in the document'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 12 from the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא talks about being first 'in the document.' That seems to contradict the claim that there are no documents.

phrases.english: But it says "whoever comes first in the document"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא כׇּל הַקּוֹדֵם בִּשְׁטָר קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that there is no document.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's own words mention a document.

steps.title: Answer: it means the dying man's instruction document
steps.stepSummary: The 'document' in the ברייתא is the dying man's written instructions, not the loan documents.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the document of instructions.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains which document the ברייתא means, and this keeps the creditor reading standing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's 'document' is the paper where the dying man wrote whom to pay and in what order. The loan documents are still missing, so the creditor reading works and the proof about gifts is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: A document of instructions written by a dying man

steps.whatToRemember: The proof from the ברייתא is pushed away. It could be about a dying man paying back creditors, who are like buyers. So it does not show that the תקנה protects a gift-receiver.

phrases.english: In the document of instructions.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁטָר פְּקַדְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 13 and finishes defending the דחיה of step 8.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Document' means the dying man's instruction document, so the proof from gifts is rejected.

steps.title: Even with gifts, only the last recipient truly loses
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: the ברייתא can be about real gifts. 'He collects from the last' only means that the last recipient is the one who ends up losing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say the ברייתא is also about a gift. It is still not difficult. What does 'he collects from the last' mean? It means only the last one loses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way to reject the proof from step 7. It keeps the ברייתא as a case of real gifts and reads the words 'collects from the last' in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the גמרא said the ברייתא is about paying debts, not gifts. Now it says it can be about gifts too. The creditor may collect from any recipient's land, but the gifts are then redivided by the order in the will, so in the end only the last recipient loses.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say: introduces another possible answer

steps.confusionAlert: 'Collects from the last' does not have to mean the creditor physically takes the last person's field. It can mean the last person is the one who ends up bearing the loss.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say: even a gift as well.
phrases.notes: He means the ברייתא can be about real gifts, not only about paying off debts.

phrases.english: And it is not difficult.
What is the meaning of 'he collects from the last'?
No one loses except the last one.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: אֲפִילּוּ מַתָּנָה נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers another answer instead of the debt-payment reading from steps 10-14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Collects from the last' means the creditor takes the last recipient's land, so the ברייתא would be a proof about gifts.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means only the last recipient loses in the end, so the ברייתא proves nothing about gifts.

steps.title: All the fields were of equal quality
steps.stepSummary: A third answer: the ברייתא is about a case where all the recipients' fields are the same quality.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: the case is where all the fields are equal to each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third answer. The ברייתא is about fields that are all the same quality.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If all the fields are the same quality, the creditor gains nothing by going to the first recipient, so collecting from the last one is no special favor to the first. That means the ברייתא tells us nothing about whether the תקנה protecting buyers (step 2) also protects gift-receivers.

keyTerms.meaning: All of them to each other

steps.whatToRemember: There are three answers to the proof from the ברייתא: (1) תנו means paying debts, (2) only the last recipient loses in the end, (3) all the fields were equal. With any of them, the ברייתא does not prove the rule applies to gifts.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
That all of them are equal to one another.
phrases.notes: He means the fields given to each person are all the same quality.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: דְּשָׁווּ כּוּלְּהוּ לַהֲדָדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another alternative answer that limits the case of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first recipient had average land, and the creditor still went to the last recipient.
steps.terutzMaskana: All the fields were equal, so collecting from the last proves nothing.

steps.title: Why no collection for eaten produce?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that sold property is not taken for produce, and asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: the court does not take sold property to pay for produce. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes a line from the משנה and asks why that rule is true, setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case: a man steals a field and sells it, and the buyer grows produce on it. The real owner takes back the field and the produce. The buyer can get back from the thief's sold property what he paid for the field, but not the value of the produce. The גמרא wants to know why.

keyTerms.meaning: The court does not take away (from buyers of sold property)
Eating of produce: the produce the buyer lost

phrases.english: We do not take away property for the eating of produce.
phrases.notes: This is a line quoted from the משנה. 'Take away' means taking it from people who bought property from the seller.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין מוֹצִיאִין לַאֲכִילַת פֵּירוֹת. מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new rule in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason sold property cannot be taken to pay for produce.

steps.title: Because the produce is not written
steps.stepSummary: עולא, quoting ריש לקיש, says the reason is that the produce is not written in the sale document.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said in the name of ריש לקיש: because they are not written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. Sold property is not taken for produce because the produce was never written in the document.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Other buyers can be made to pay only for debts that are written down, because written debts are publicly known. The seller's duty to pay back for produce is not in the sale document, so it is like an unwritten loan. Later buyers could not have known about it.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who often reports teachings from ארץ ישראל
A great אמורא of ארץ ישראל

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a general idea: only written, publicly known debts can be collected from property that was sold. The next step tests this idea.

phrases.english: Ulla said that Reish Lakish said:
Because they are not written.
phrases.notes: 'They' means the produce, which is not listed in the sale document.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The produce is not written in the document, so later buyers are not responsible for it.

steps.title: Support for wife and daughters counts as written, yet is not collected
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא challenges עולא: the support of a wife and daughters counts as if it were written, and yet the משנה says it is not collected from sold property.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said to עולא: But the support of the wife and daughters is treated as if it were written, and still the משנה teaches that we do not take sold property for it!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא attacks עולא's reason. He points to a case where the debt counts as written, yet the משנה still does not allow collection from sold property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband's duty to feed his wife and daughters is a fixed condition of every כתובה, so it counts as written even if it is not spelled out. If 'not written' were the only reason, this support should be collectable from sold property. Since the משנה says it is not, 'not written' does not seem to be the real reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Support (food) of the wife and daughters
They are treated as if they were written

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said to Ulla:
But the support of the wife and the daughters,
which are treated as if they were written,
phrases.notes: Supporting them is a standard condition of every כתובה, so it counts as written even when it isn't spelled out.

phrases.english: And yet it teaches: we do not take away property for them!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא לְעוּלָּא: וְהָא מְזוֹן הָאִשָּׁה וְהַבָּנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's reason in the name of ריש לקיש: 'because they are not written.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Support of wife and daughters counts as written, yet the משנה still does not collect it from sold property. So 'not written' cannot be the whole reason.

steps.title: Support was set up to count as written only for property still owned
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers רבי אבא: חכמים arranged from the start that the support of a wife and daughters counts as written for free property, but not for sold property.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There, it was set up this way from the start. They count as written for free property, but they do not count as written for sold property.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא defends his reason ('produce is not written') against רבי אבא's challenge from step 19.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבא argued that support of a wife and daughters counts as written, yet it still cannot be taken from sold property. עולא answers that this 'counts as written' status was limited from the very beginning: it applies only to property the man still owns (בני חורין), not to property he sold (משועבדין). So the support case does not break his rule.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start it was set up this way (by חכמים)
Written (counted as if written in the document)
Free property, still owned by the debtor
Sold property that is under a lien

steps.confusionAlert: The support is not 'unwritten' across the board. It counts as written, but only for property the man still owns; the limit was built into the original rule.

phrases.english: He said to him: There,
phrases.notes: עולא is answering רבי אבא. 'There' means the case of the support of a wife and daughters.

phrases.english: from the start it was set up this way –
they count as written regarding free property,
but they do not count as written regarding sold property.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָתָם, מֵעִיקָּרָא הָכִי אִתַּקּוּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אבא's challenge in step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the challenging case: its 'written' status was restricted from the start.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Support of a wife and daughters counts as written everywhere, so it should be collectible from sold property, which would disprove the 'not written' reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'written' status of support was set up from the start to apply only to free property, so the 'not written' reason still stands.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן gives the same 'not written' reason
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי, quoting רבי יוחנן, also says produce is not taken from sold property because it is not written.
steps.simpleTranslation: And likewise, רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: It is because they are not written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second source that gives the same reason as עולא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now רבי יוחנן, through רבי אסי, also explains the משנה's rule: the produce is not written in the sale document. This adds a second, separate voice backing the 'not written' reason.

keyTerms.meaning: And likewise said (introduces a matching opinion)
רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And likewise, Rabbi Asi said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
because they are not written.
phrases.notes: He means the produce is not written in the buyer's sale document.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second source agreeing with עולא's reason in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Produce is not collected from sold property because it is not written in the sale document.

steps.title: רבי זירא raises the support challenge against רבי אסי
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא challenges רבי אסי: the support of a wife and daughters counts as written, yet the משנה says it is not collected from sold property.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to רב אסי: But the support of a wife and daughters is treated as if written, and yet the משנה teaches that it is not collected!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא attacks רבי אסי's 'not written' reason with the same case רבי אבא used against עולא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'written' is what allows collection from sold property, then support, which counts as written, should be collectible. But the משנה says it is not. So 'written' does not seem to be the real deciding factor.

keyTerms.meaning: Support (food and needs) of a wife and daughters
Which are treated as if they were written
We do not collect (from sold property)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַב אַסִּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to Rav Asi:
But the support of the wife and the daughters,
which are treated as if written,
and yet it teaches: we do not collect!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַב אַסִּי: וְהָא מְזוֹן הָאִשָּׁה וְהַבָּנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given by רבי אסי in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אסי's report of רבי יוחנן's reason, 'because they are not written'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Support counts as written but still cannot be taken from sold property, so being written cannot be what decides it.

steps.title: רבי אסי gives the same answer: support was limited from the start
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי answers just like עולא: support was set up to count as written only for free property, not for sold property.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: From the start it was set up this way. They count as written for free property, but not for sold property.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי answers רבי זירא's challenge with the exact same answer עולא gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Support's 'written' status was always limited to property the man still owns. So it was never counted as written for sold property, and the 'not written' reason stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: He said to him (introduces the reply)

steps.whatToRemember: Both עולא and רבי יוחנן hold that produce is not collected from sold property because it is not written. The support case fits, because its 'written' status was limited from the start to free property.

phrases.english: He said to him: from the start it was set up this way –
they count as written regarding free property,
but they do not count as written regarding sold property.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מֵעִיקָּרָא הָכִי אִתַּקּוּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's challenge in step 22, using the same answer as step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the challenging case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Support counts as written for all property, which would disprove the 'not written' reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: Support counts as written only for free property, so the 'not written' reason holds.

steps.title: רבי חנינא: produce is not a fixed amount
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא gives a different reason: produce is not collected from sold property because its amount is not fixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: It is because they are not fixed.
steps.whatsHappening: A new reason is offered for the משנה's rule, different from 'not written'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי חנינא, the issue is that nobody knows ahead of time how much produce will grow or what it will be worth. Because the amount is not set, it cannot be collected from sold property.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives a different reason
Because they are not a fixed amount

steps.whyThisMatters: This opens a second approach to the משנה, and the גמרא will next ask how it relates to the 'not written' reason.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין קְצוּבִין.
phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina said: because they are not fixed.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין קְצוּבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the question in step 17 than עולא and רבי יוחנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Produce is not collected from sold property because its amount is not fixed.

steps.title: Does רבי חנינא need both fixed and written?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to ask: according to רבי חנינא, must a debt be both fixed and written to be collected from sold property?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: According to רבי חנינא, does he require both fixed and written?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a question about how far רבי חנינא's reason goes; the rest of the question continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether רבי חנינא adds 'fixed' on top of רבי יוחנן's 'written' requirement, so that both are needed. The other side of the question is not yet stated here.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked by them (an open question)

phrases.english: A question was raised before them: according to Rabbi Ḥanina –
does he require fixed and written,

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: לְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how רבי חנינא's reason in step 24 relates to the 'written' requirement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי חנינא requires a debt to be both fixed and written in order to be collected from sold property.
